# cloudtower Provider



## Example Usage

```terraform
# Configure the provider for a CloudTower with a single management endpoint.
# The server address accepts an optional scheme and defaults to http.
provider "cloudtower" {
  cloudtower_server = "https://tower.example.com"
  username          = "admin"
  password          = "password"
  user_source       = "LOCAL"
}

# For an HA CloudTower (4.9.0+, multiple management IPs in an active-passive
# deployment), configure every management endpoint of the cluster instead of
# cloudtower_server. The provider probes the endpoints to find the active node
# and fails over automatically when the active node switches.
#
# provider "cloudtower" {
#   cloudtower_servers = ["https://tower-a.example.com", "https://tower-b.example.com"]
#   username           = "admin"
#   password           = "password"
#   user_source        = "LOCAL"
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `password` (String) The user password for CloudTower API operations.
- `user_source` (String) The source type of user
- `username` (String) The username for CloudTower API operations.

### Optional

- `cloudtower_server` (String) The CloudTower server address, e.g. `tower.example.com` or `https://tower.example.com`. For an HA CloudTower use `cloudtower_servers` instead.
- `cloudtower_servers` (List of String) The management endpoints of an HA CloudTower (4.9.0+, multiple management IPs in an active-passive deployment), e.g. `["https://tower-a.example.com", "https://tower-b.example.com"]`. The provider probes the endpoints to find the active node and fails over automatically when the active node switches. Conflicts with `cloudtower_server`.
